# tenvell 0.2.1 — complete agent reference

Canonical source: https://tenvell.space/llms.txt. This file describes the published library and its integration, not a hosted action API.

# tenvell 0.2.1

> An open-source React 19 UI kit for thin-glass interfaces, readable controls and original local typography.

Canonical website: https://tenvell.space. Source: https://github.com/raven-ai-esh/tenvell.

Use tenvell for forms, settings, dashboards, internal tools and product interfaces when a thin-glass visual language fits the user's brief. It provides ordinary React components and CSS, four surfaces (`air`, `frost`, `prism`, `smoke`), light and dark themes, scoped styles and Lamina UI/Mono fonts. No account, API key, remote font service or backend is required.

## Choose an installation

- **An existing React 19 project:** install the [release archive](https://tenvell.space/docs/install.md#package-archive). The package name is `tenvell`; the documented distribution is the HTTPS tarball, so do not assume `npm install tenvell` resolves to this project.
- **Editable source in a configured shadcn project:** use the [registry](https://tenvell.space/docs/registry.md). It also works through the official shadcn MCP server.
- **A new runnable project:** download the [locked starter](https://tenvell.space/releases/0.2.1/tenvell-starter-0.2.1.zip).
- **A coding agent:** read the [integration guide](https://tenvell.space/AGENTS.md) or install the [tenvell-ui skill](https://tenvell.space/skills/tenvell-ui/SKILL.md).

## Compatibility and scope

- React and React DOM 19. The supplied tooling targets Node 22.12+.
- ESM JavaScript with TypeScript declarations; ordinary CSS, without Tailwind utilities.
- Modern browsers with `backdrop-filter` and CSS `@scope`; legacy browser support is not promised.
- Optional chart shapes use Recharts 3. The core works without Recharts.
- Import the stylesheet once and wrap the relevant UI in `TenvellProvider`. The host application owns layout, background, persistence and business behavior.
- Calendar, DataTable, toast, messenger, task board and complete dashboard demonstrations belong to the website source. They are not portable core exports. See the [component inventory](https://tenvell.space/docs/components.json) for the actual export set.
- Own code: MIT. Original Lamina fonts: SIL OFL 1.1. Preserve the bundled notices when distributing copied source or fonts.

## Documentation

- [Choosing a React UI kit](https://tenvell.space/choosing-a-react-ui-kit)
- [Glassmorphism interfaces](https://tenvell.space/react-glassmorphism-ui-kit)
- [Dashboards and settings](https://tenvell.space/react-dashboard-ui-kit)
- [Editable shadcn glass components](https://tenvell.space/shadcn-glass-components)
- [Install and first component](https://tenvell.space/docs/install.md)
- [Published API and provider settings](https://tenvell.space/docs/api.md)
- [Registry and MCP](https://tenvell.space/docs/registry.md)
- [Working interface recipes](https://tenvell.space/docs/recipes.md)
- [Full reference in one request](https://tenvell.space/llms-full.txt)
- [Interactive catalog](https://tenvell.space/)

The demonstrations use fictional local data. Their UI actions do not send messages, create accounts, connect a CRM or supply a production backend.


---

# Install tenvell 0.2.1

Requires React/React DOM 19 and a modern browser with CSS `@scope` and `backdrop-filter`. Use Node 22.12+ for the supplied tooling.

## Package archive

In an existing React 19 application:

```sh
npm install https://tenvell.space/releases/0.2.1/tenvell-0.2.1.tgz
```

This installs the package from the official website. A plain `npm install tenvell` is not the documented distribution channel.

Import the stylesheet once at your application's entrypoint. In frameworks that restrict global CSS imports, place it in the permitted root layout or entry file. Components use client-side interactions; in a React Server Components project, put the component using hooks or event handlers behind a `"use client"` boundary.

```jsx
import { TenvellProvider, Button, Card, Input } from 'tenvell';
import 'tenvell/styles.css';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <TenvellProvider theme="light" surface="air">
      <Card>
        <label htmlFor="name">Name</label>
        <Input id="name" name="name" placeholder="Your name" />
        <Button type="button">Continue</Button>
      </Card>
    </TenvellProvider>
  );
}
```

The button is an interface element; connect its action to your application's behavior.

## Editable source through shadcn

In a React 19 project with a working `components.json` and aliases:

```sh
npx shadcn@4.23.0 add https://tenvell.space/r/tenvell.json
```

With the conventional `@/*` alias pointing to your source directory:

```jsx
import { TenvellProvider, Button, Card } from '@/components/tenvell';
import '@/components/tenvell/styles.css';
```

The CLI copies editable components, CSS and licences. Keep your existing shadcn configuration and adjust the imports if its `components` alias differs. The copied tenvell components use ordinary CSS; do not replace their styles with Tailwind utilities.

To start with a small runnable example instead of the full core:

```sh
npx shadcn@4.23.0 add https://tenvell.space/r/button-demo.json
```

```jsx
import ButtonDemo from '@/components/tenvell/examples/button-demo';

export default function App() {
  return <ButtonDemo />;
}
```

For individual items, use their documented module imports. For example `button.json` exports `Button`, `Input`, `Textarea` and `TenvellProvider` from `@/components/tenvell/button`; it does not install the full core barrel. See the [registry reference](https://tenvell.space/docs/registry.md).

## Locked starter

Download [tenvell-starter-0.2.1.zip](https://tenvell.space/releases/0.2.1/tenvell-starter-0.2.1.zip), extract it into a new folder and run:

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

To check TypeScript and build the starter:

```sh
npm run build
```

The starter includes the package tarball, a lockfile and a local example. It has no production backend.

## Optional charts

For the package installation:

```sh
npm install recharts@3.10.1
```

```jsx
import { GlassBar, GlassDot, GlassSector } from 'tenvell/charts';
```

For copied source, install `https://tenvell.space/r/charts.json` and import from `@/components/tenvell/charts`. Use the shapes inside Recharts components. See [recipes](https://tenvell.space/docs/recipes.md).

## Verify the release

The [release manifest](https://tenvell.space/releases/0.2.1/manifest.json) contains filenames, byte lengths and SHA-256 checksums. The package, starter and source archives are immutable published artifacts. Documentation updates do not replace their bytes.

If a UI appears unstyled, check the stylesheet import and provider before adding CSS. If an import is missing, check the [published API](https://tenvell.space/docs/api.md) and whether you installed an individual registry item or the complete core.


---

# tenvell 0.2.1 API

The declarations below are extracted from the published package archive. They describe the installed release, including exact export names and component props.

## Provider

`TenvellProvider` renders a scoped wrapper. Import `tenvell/styles.css` once; the provider does not set the host page's layout or background and does not persist application preferences.

| Prop | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `light`, `dark` | `light` |
| `surface` | `air`, `frost`, `prism`, `smoke` | `air` |
| `accent` | `slate`, `blue`, `violet`, `jade` | `slate` |
| `radius` | `strict`, `soft`, `round` | `soft` |
| `density` | `comfortable`, `compact` | `comfortable` |
| `motion` | boolean | `true` |

Multiple independent providers are supported. Dialogs and menus inherit their originating provider's theme through a body portal. CSS custom properties passed in the provider's `style` also reach its overlays; layout styles stay on the wrapper. `--tenvell-overlay-z` sets the overlay layer (default `1000`). Reduced-motion preferences take precedence.

Pass product labels and accessible names explicitly. The portable core renders caller-provided content; the website's EN/RU translation layer is not part of the package.

## Export boundaries

- `tenvell`: the core exports shown below.
- `tenvell/styles.css`: scoped styles and locally embedded Lamina fonts.
- `tenvell/charts`: optional Recharts shapes, with Recharts 3 installed separately.
- Website-only examples include Calendar, DataTable, toast, the messenger, task board and complete product screens. Do not import these names from the core package.

After a source-first installation, substitute the corresponding `@/components/tenvell` module paths. The compact [component inventory](https://tenvell.space/docs/components.json) records the exports of each registry item.

## Core TypeScript declarations

```ts
import type * as React from 'react';
import {Dialog as D} from '@base-ui/react/dialog';
import {Menu as M} from '@base-ui/react/menu';
import {Tabs as T} from '@base-ui/react/tabs';
import {Accordion as A} from '@base-ui/react/accordion';
import {Popover as P} from '@base-ui/react/popover';
import {Checkbox as C} from '@base-ui/react/checkbox';
import {Switch as S} from '@base-ui/react/switch';
import {Select as SelectBase} from '@base-ui/react/select';

type Styled<T>=Omit<T,'className'>&{className?:string};
export type Theme='light'|'dark';
export type Surface='air'|'frost'|'prism'|'smoke';
export type Accent='slate'|'blue'|'violet'|'jade';
export type Radius='strict'|'soft'|'round';
export type Density='comfortable'|'compact';
export interface TenvellProviderProps extends Omit<React.ComponentProps<'div'>,'style'>{theme?:Theme;surface?:Surface;accent?:Accent;radius?:Radius;density?:Density;motion?:boolean;style?:React.CSSProperties&Record<`--${string}`,string|number|undefined>}
export function TenvellProvider(props:TenvellProviderProps):React.JSX.Element;
export interface ButtonProps extends React.ComponentProps<'button'>{variant?:'primary'|'secondary'|'outline'|'ghost'|'icon'|'link'|'destructive';size?:'default'|'sm'|'lg'|'icon';loading?:boolean}
export function Button(props:ButtonProps):React.JSX.Element;
export function Input(props:React.ComponentProps<'input'>):React.JSX.Element;
export function Textarea(props:React.ComponentProps<'textarea'>):React.JSX.Element;
export function Checkbox(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof C.Root>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function Switch(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof S.Root>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function Card(props:React.ComponentProps<'article'>&{surface?:Surface}):React.JSX.Element;
export function CardHeader(props:React.ComponentProps<'header'>):React.JSX.Element;
export function CardTitle(props:React.ComponentProps<'h3'>):React.JSX.Element;
export function CardDescription(props:React.ComponentProps<'p'>):React.JSX.Element;
export function CardContent(props:React.ComponentProps<'div'>):React.JSX.Element;
export function CardFooter(props:React.ComponentProps<'footer'>):React.JSX.Element;
export const glassMaterials:{id:Surface;name:string;description:string}[];
export type GlassSurfaceProps<Element extends React.ElementType='div'>={as?:Element;surface?:Surface;className?:string}&Omit<React.ComponentPropsWithRef<Element>,'as'|'surface'|'className'>;
export function GlassSurface<Element extends React.ElementType='div'>(props:GlassSurfaceProps<Element>):React.JSX.Element;
export function GlassPicker(props:{value:Surface;onChange:(value:Surface)=>void;label?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export interface SelectProps extends Omit<Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof SelectBase.Trigger>>,'value'|'onChange'|'name'>{items:{value:string;label:React.ReactNode}[];name?:string;value?:string|null;onValueChange?:(value:string|null)=>void}
export function Select(props:SelectProps):React.JSX.Element;
export const Dialog:typeof D.Root;
export const DialogTrigger:typeof D.Trigger;
export const DialogClose:typeof D.Close;
export function DialogTitle(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof D.Title>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function DialogDescription(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof D.Description>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function DialogContent(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof D.Popup>>):React.JSX.Element|null;
export const DropdownMenu:typeof M.Root;
export const DropdownMenuTrigger:typeof M.Trigger;
export const DropdownMenuGroup:typeof M.Group;
export const DropdownMenuRadioGroup:typeof M.RadioGroup;
export function DropdownMenuContent(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof M.Popup>>&{align?:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof M.Positioner>>['align']}):React.JSX.Element;
export function DropdownMenuItem(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof M.Item>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function DropdownMenuLabel(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof M.GroupLabel>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function DropdownMenuSeparator(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof M.Separator>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function DropdownMenuCheckboxItem(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof M.CheckboxItem>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function DropdownMenuRadioItem(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof M.RadioItem>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function Tabs(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof T.Root>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function TabsList(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof T.List>>&{variant?:'segmented'|'line'|'vertical'}):React.JSX.Element;
export function TabsTrigger(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof T.Tab>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function TabsContent(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof T.Panel>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function Accordion(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof A.Root>>):React.JSX.Element;
export const AccordionItem:typeof A.Item;
export function AccordionTrigger(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof A.Trigger>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function AccordionContent(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof A.Panel>>):React.JSX.Element;
export const Popover:typeof P.Root;
export const PopoverTrigger:typeof P.Trigger;
export const PopoverClose:typeof P.Close;
export const PopoverTitle:typeof P.Title;
export const PopoverDescription:typeof P.Description;
export function PopoverContent(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof P.Popup>>&{align?:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof P.Positioner>>['align']}):React.JSX.Element;
export function Tooltip(props:{children:React.ReactElement<{'aria-describedby'?:string}>;content:React.ReactNode;side?:'top'|'right'|'bottom'|'left'}):React.JSX.Element;
export const Sheet:typeof D.Root;
export const SheetTrigger:typeof D.Trigger;
export const SheetClose:typeof D.Close;
export const SheetTitle:typeof D.Title;
export const SheetDescription:typeof D.Description;
export function SheetContent(props:Styled<React.ComponentProps<typeof D.Popup>>):React.JSX.Element;
export function Combobox(props:{items:string[];value?:string|null;onValueChange:(value:string|null)=>void;label?:string;placeholder?:string;disabled?:boolean}):React.JSX.Element;
export function Badge(props:React.ComponentProps<'span'>&{tone?:'neutral'|'success'|'warning'|'info'|'error'}):React.JSX.Element;
export function Avatar(props:{fallback?:React.ReactNode;alt?:string;src?:string;size?:'default'|'sm'|'lg';className?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export function AvatarGroup(props:{children?:React.ReactNode;label?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export function Separator(props:React.ComponentProps<'div'>&{orientation?:'horizontal'|'vertical'}):React.JSX.Element;
export function Skeleton(props:React.ComponentProps<'div'>):React.JSX.Element;
export function Progress(props:Omit<React.ComponentProps<'progress'>,'value'>&{value?:number|null;max?:number;label?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export function EmptyState(props:React.ComponentProps<'div'>&{title?:string;description?:React.ReactNode;icon?:React.ElementType}):React.JSX.Element;
export function InputGroup(props:React.ComponentProps<'div'>):React.JSX.Element;
export function InputAddon(props:{children?:React.ReactNode;align?:'start'|'end';className?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export function ButtonGroup(props:{children?:React.ReactNode;label?:string;className?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export function RadioGroup(props:{items:{value:string;label:React.ReactNode;description?:React.ReactNode;disabled?:boolean}[];value:string;onValueChange:(value:string)=>void;label?:string;name?:string;disabled?:boolean;className?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export function Slider(props:Omit<React.ComponentProps<'input'>,'value'|'onChange'|'min'|'max'|'step'>&{value?:number;onValueChange:(value:number)=>void;min?:number;max?:number;step?:number;label?:string;unit?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export function Breadcrumb(props:{items:{label:React.ReactNode;href?:string}[];label?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export function Pagination(props:{page:number;pages:number;onPageChange:(page:number)=>void;label?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
export function ToggleGroup(props:{items:{value:string;label:string;icon?:React.ElementType}[];value:string;onValueChange:(value:string)=>void;label?:string}):React.JSX.Element;
```

import type * as React from 'react';

export interface GlassBarProps{x?:number;y?:number;width?:number;height?:number;radius?:number|[number,number,number,number];fill?:string;index?:number;value?:number|[number,number];active?:boolean;isActive?:boolean}
export function GlassBar(props:GlassBarProps):React.JSX.Element|null;
export function GlassDot(props:{cx?:number;cy?:number;fill?:string;stroke?:string}):React.JSX.Element|null;

# tenvell registry and MCP

The [public registry index](https://tenvell.space/r/registry.json) lists installable source items. Item URLs return the shadcn registry format, including editable source and dependencies; no authentication is required.

## Namespace

Merge this field into the existing `components.json` in a configured React 19/shadcn project. Preserve the project's other settings and aliases.

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@tenvell": "https://tenvell.space/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

Then install the complete core or a smaller working example:

```sh
npx shadcn@4.23.0 add @tenvell/tenvell
npx shadcn@4.23.0 add @tenvell/button-demo
```

Either command is an alternative starting point; running both is unnecessary. Without a namespace mapping, use the full item URL from the table below.

## Official shadcn MCP server

The [official shadcn MCP server](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/mcp) reads your project's registry configuration and supports listing, searching, viewing and installing compatible registry items. In clients using the common `mcpServers` configuration shape, the server entry is:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "shadcn": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["shadcn@4.23.0", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Client configuration locations differ; use the official guide for your client. Run the server in the context of the target project so it can read `components.json`. Installing this configuration is a user choice; reading this website does not modify the client's settings.

With `@tenvell` configured, an example request is:

> Find the button, card and dialog components in the @tenvell registry, inspect their APIs, and build a React 19 settings form with a light air surface. Keep the existing application routing and connect the save action to local form state.

Tenvell provides the static registry. The MCP process is the official shadcn CLI running in the consumer's environment; the website does not advertise a separate hosted MCP endpoint.

## Items and imports

The following table is generated from the current published registry. `@/components` assumes the conventional project alias; use your configured components alias when it differs. Import `@/components/tenvell/styles.css` once after installing source items.

| Item | Purpose | Import from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [tenvell](https://tenvell.space/r/tenvell.json) | A complete React 19 UI kit for glassmorphism dashboards, settings and forms. Scoped CSS, original local fonts, cards, fields, menus and dialogs. | `@/components/tenvell` |
| [provider](https://tenvell.space/r/provider.json) | Independent light and dark themes, four glass surfaces, accents, radius, density and motion settings for a React UI scope and its overlays. | `@/components/tenvell/provider` |
| [button](https://tenvell.space/r/button.json) | React buttons, text inputs and textareas for forms and product actions, with thin-glass styling and loading or disabled states. | `@/components/tenvell/button` |
| [checkbox](https://tenvell.space/r/checkbox.json) | A thin-glass React checkbox for settings and forms, including checked, unchecked and indeterminate states. | `@/components/tenvell/checkbox` |
| [switch](https://tenvell.space/r/switch.json) | A thin-glass React switch for on/off preferences and settings panels. | `@/components/tenvell/switch` |
| [card](https://tenvell.space/r/card.json) | Composable thin-glass React cards for dashboard metrics, profile panels and grouped settings, with header, content and footer parts. | `@/components/tenvell/card` |
| [glass](https://tenvell.space/r/glass.json) | Four glassmorphism surface finishes and a material picker for React interfaces, with light and dark themes and scoped styling. | `@/components/tenvell/glass` |
| [select](https://tenvell.space/r/select.json) | A themed React select control for form fields and dashboard filters, with a provider-scoped popup. | `@/components/tenvell/select` |
| [menu](https://tenvell.space/r/menu.json) | React dropdown menus for product actions and settings, with themed portalled content and selection items. | `@/components/tenvell/menu` |
| [dialog](https://tenvell.space/r/dialog.json) | React modal dialogs with thin-glass styling, accessible titles and descriptions, and the originating provider’s theme. | `@/components/tenvell/dialog` |
| [primitives](https://tenvell.space/r/primitives.json) | React identity, selection, navigation and feedback controls, including badges, avatars, progress, radio groups and pagination. | `@/components/tenvell/primitives` |
| [disclosure](https://tenvell.space/r/disclosure.json) | React tabs, accordion, popover, tooltip, side sheet and combobox components for navigation, details and product forms. | `@/components/tenvell/disclosure` |
| [charts](https://tenvell.space/r/charts.json) | Optional Recharts 3 shapes for glass bars, dots and sectors in React dashboards. Item highlighting follows the actual chart element. | `@/components/tenvell/charts` |
| [button-demo](https://tenvell.space/r/button-demo.json) | A runnable button example with its provider, scoped styles, click feedback and light/dark toggle. | `@/components/tenvell/examples/button-demo` |

A source item includes its provider dependency and scoped CSS. Installing several overlapping items may prompt the CLI about existing files; review changes in the target project. The complete core is usually the simplest option when several component families are needed.


---

# tenvell interface recipes

These examples use the package installation from the [install guide](https://tenvell.space/docs/install.md). For the complete source-first core, substitute `@/components/tenvell` and `@/components/tenvell/styles.css`.

## A working settings form

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  TenvellProvider, Card, CardHeader, CardTitle,
  CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter, Input, Button
} from 'tenvell';
import 'tenvell/styles.css';

export default function SettingsForm() {
  const [name, setName] = useState('Alex');
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(false);

  function submit(event) {
    event.preventDefault();
    setSaved(true);
  }

  return (
    <TenvellProvider theme="light" surface="air" accent="slate">
      <form onSubmit={submit} style={{ maxWidth: 480, margin: '2rem auto' }}>
        <Card>
          <CardHeader>
            <CardTitle>Profile</CardTitle>
            <CardDescription>Your name in this local preview.</CardDescription>
          </CardHeader>
          <CardContent>
            <label htmlFor="profile-name">Display name</label>
            <Input id="profile-name" value={name} required
              onChange={event => { setName(event.target.value); setSaved(false); }} />
          </CardContent>
          <CardFooter>
            <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
            <span role="status">{saved ? 'Saved in this view' : ''}</span>
          </CardFooter>
        </Card>
      </form>
    </TenvellProvider>
  );
}
```

This deliberately keeps data in React state. Add persistence or a network request only when the application requires it.

## A controlled dialog

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  TenvellProvider, Button, Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent,
  DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogClose
} from 'tenvell';
import 'tenvell/styles.css';

export default function DetailsDialog() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <TenvellProvider theme="dark" surface="frost">
      <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Open details</DialogTrigger>
        <DialogContent>
          <DialogTitle>Details</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>This dialog inherits its provider's theme.</DialogDescription>
          <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Close</DialogClose>
        </DialogContent>
      </Dialog>
    </TenvellProvider>
  );
}
```

Triggers use the Base UI `render` prop. Do not assume a Radix `asChild` API. The provider supplies the themed body portal; do not move the dialog out of its originating provider to apply a theme.

## A Recharts bar shape

Install `recharts@3.10.1` separately. Use the glass shapes as actual chart elements:

```jsx
import { BarChart, Bar, XAxis, YAxis, Tooltip, ResponsiveContainer } from 'recharts';
import { TenvellProvider } from 'tenvell';
import { GlassBar } from 'tenvell/charts';
import 'tenvell/styles.css';

const data = [{ day: 'Mon', value: 12 }, { day: 'Tue', value: 19 }];

export default function ActivityChart() {
  return (
    <TenvellProvider theme="light" surface="air">
      <div style={{ height: 280, minWidth: 0 }}>
        <ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height="100%">
          <BarChart data={data}>
            <XAxis dataKey="day" />
            <YAxis />
            <Tooltip cursor={false} />
            <Bar dataKey="value" shape={<GlassBar />} activeBar={<GlassBar />} />
          </BarChart>
        </ResponsiveContainer>
      </div>
    </TenvellProvider>
  );
}
```

The host application provides a nonzero chart height. Keep `Tooltip cursor={false}` so hover follows the actual bar rather than a rectangular overlay. The starter contains a complete working chart.


---

# Use tenvell with a coding agent

This document is guidance for integrating tenvell 0.2.1 into a consumer project. Follow the user's requested stack, design and repository instructions. The contributor instructions for tenvell itself are in the repository's [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/raven-ai-esh/tenvell/blob/main/AGENTS.md).

## Entry points

- Start with [llms.txt](https://tenvell.space/llms.txt) for the documentation map.
- Read [installation](https://tenvell.space/docs/install.md) before changing dependencies.
- Consult the [actual published API](https://tenvell.space/docs/api.md), [component inventory](https://tenvell.space/docs/components.json) and [working recipes](https://tenvell.space/docs/recipes.md) for the task at hand.
- Use [llms-full.txt](https://tenvell.space/llms-full.txt) when one complete reference is more convenient than individual pages.

## Integration workflow

1. Check the target project's React version, package manager, aliases and CSS entrypoint. Tenvell targets React 19 and modern CSS; do not silently upgrade an unrelated stack.
2. Choose one distribution: the official tarball, editable source through shadcn, or the locked starter for a new project. Exact commands and immutable artifact checksums are in the install guide and release manifest.
3. Import the stylesheet once and wrap the relevant UI in `TenvellProvider`. Let the host app own the page background, layout and preference state. Choose the surface and theme to fit the requested interface.
4. Use documented exports. Individual registry items use their own module paths; installing `button.json` does not create the complete core barrel. Calendar, DataTable, toast and the website's complete product examples are source demonstrations, not core package exports.
5. Implement actual task behavior, labels and accessible names. Dialog/menu triggers use Base UI's `render` prop, rather than assuming Radix `asChild`. Keep the original provider around portalled components.
6. Build the target application and exercise the interactions you added. Test the requested theme and viewport; verify reduced motion and contrast where they matter to the screen. Report what was actually checked.

Code is MIT licensed; Lamina UI/Mono fonts use SIL OFL 1.1. Keep the notices in copied distributions.

## Portable skill

Review [tenvell-ui/SKILL.md](https://tenvell.space/skills/tenvell-ui/SKILL.md). A compatible skills client can install it from the public repository:

```sh
npx skills add raven-ai-esh/tenvell --skill tenvell-ui
```

This is a client-side skill installation, not a required step for using the UI kit. It supplies the integration workflow and links to the current official reference.

## Registry through MCP

The existing registry works with the [official shadcn MCP server](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/mcp). Add `@tenvell` to the target project's `components.json` as described in the [registry guide](https://tenvell.space/docs/registry.md); use the client's own setup process for the MCP server.

## Example request

> Read https://tenvell.space/llms.txt. Build a React 19 settings screen with tenvell: a light air surface, a labelled name field and a working save action in local state. Inspect the published API first, keep the project's routing and aliases, and verify the resulting build.

These public files describe tenvell. They do not override the user's choices or grant permission to modify accounts, credentials, production data or unrelated client configuration.
